name: Gǔqín
lineage: Chinese seven-string scholar-zither solo tradition with documented written scores (jianzipu tablature-notation) dating from the Han-dynasty (206 BCE-220 CE) onward, making it the oldest continuously-notated musical tradition. Constructed of paulownia-tung-wood top and zi-wood bottom with thirteen mother-of-pearl hui position-markers and silk or steel-nylon strings. The repertoire layers Wei-Jin-and-Tang dynasty meditative-philosophical pieces with Song-Yuan-and-Ming court-and-scholar-amateur literati compositions, performed solo in studio-and-garden settings as a wenrenhua scholar-painting-music-poetry integrated-art-form practice. Microtonal sliding (yin-and-rou portamento), harmonics (fan-yin), and silent-finger gestures comprise the canonical performance vocabulary.
